html:
Moldovan wine is made from one of the densest vineyard areas in the world, and wine has long been among Moldova's main exports. Vines grew here in antiquity, and the monasteries of Moldavia kept the craft alive.

Under Russian rule after 1812, nobles and German colonists planted French grapes. In Soviet times Moldova supplied a large share of the Union's wine and brandy, and limestone quarries near Chișinău became huge cellars: Cricova and Mileștii Mici hold millions of bottles in tunnels many kilometres long. When Russia banned Moldovan wine in 2006 and again in 2013, makers turned to Europe and to quality. The trade shows how Moldova's economy is caught between Russia and the European Union.
